To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The precipitation behaviour of Al–Si alloy during cooling from solution treatment is strongly dependent on cooling rate.
the precipitation behaviour of binary aluminium-silicon alloys during the cooling from solution annealed state is strongly affected by cooling rate.
the precipitation behaviour of Al–Si alloy is cooling rate dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of non-equilibrium solute content and quench induced precipitates on the mechanical properties of Al–Si alloy.
the development of a novel experimental approach to investigate the mechanical behaviour of Al–Si during cooling.
the development of an experimental approach to study mechanical properties of well defined undercooled Al-Si alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flow stress of undercooled Al-Si states is determined by the solute Si amount and the precipitates formed during cooling.
the flow stress during cooling from the solution annealed state is a function of the solute Si content, the precipitate volume fraction and the particle size.
the mechanical properties are determined by the solute content and the microstructural features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the precipitation kinetics of Al-Si alloys is strongly dependent on cooling rate.

the mechanical behaviour of undercooled states of Al–SI alloys can be predicted by the presented model for solute content calculation, and by the knowledge of the precipitation behaviour during cooling.
the precipitation behaviour during quenching from solution annealing is strongly influenced by the cooling rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of Al–Si can be tailored by the cooling rate during quenching.
the cooling rate has a major influence on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Al–Si alloy.
the cooling rate dependent formation of quench-induced precipitate particles is a crucial aspect to understand the mechanical properties of Al–Si during cooling from solution-annealing.
